heading: Therapeutic Approach
intro: Grounded in evidence-based practice, I draw from several clinical frameworks to provide the most effective support for every individual and their circumstances.

items.title: Psychodynamic
items.description: Works with the understanding that present difficulties are influenced by unconscious processes and previous life experiences. Psychodynamic therapy creates space to explore your patterns, defence mechanisms and emotional history, and how these may impact you in the present.

items.title: Trauma-Informed
items.description: This framework prioritises sensitivity and collaborative sessions to acknowledge and address trauma and its role in mental health. There is a focus on creating a therapeutic environment that is safe, honest and understanding. You are the priority, and have control over the pace and direction of sessions, so the therapeutic work can provide effective support and empowerment.

items.title: Systemic
items.description: This technique is designed to support emotional and personal growth by identifying unconscious patterns of language and behaviour. The process aims to release limiting beliefs and emotional blocks to create lasting changes. The therapeutic work allows exploration of patterns by understanding the past, to begin implementing positive change in the present and future. This may also include genograms to look into family dynamics and relationships.

items.title: Integrative
items.description: Integrative practice draws upon elements from many therapeutic frameworks (such as the systemic and humanistic approaches) to provide support tailored to each individual. Mental health support is not "one-size-fits-all" so the integrative approach can adapt to everyone.
